editorial:
Imagine failing your big high school exams and instead of telling your parents, you just make up a wild lie to get a free vacation. That is exactly what happens to Chicken and Curry. These two are best friends who do everything together, and their plan to fake a spiritual crisis to visit India is honestly pretty genius. You get to follow them as they go from being scared teenagers to people who actually start understanding the world. The vibe is light and funny at first, but it slowly turns into a sweet story about growing up and finding out where you actually belong.

What really makes this work is how the characters change. Watching Curry connect with his roots and Chicken fall for a doctor is heartwarming. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow, but the scenery makes up for it. If you are in the mood for a feel-good story, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, the lie finally catches up with them, but it does not really matter anymore. Curry finds a new sense of peace and identity after connecting with his biological sister and the culture of India. Chicken grows up too, realizing that life is bigger than her small town. They return home not as failures, but as more mature people who have finally learned how to fly on their own.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship and discovering yourself.
